 J U D G M E N T

This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of .15,00,000/- along with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by her in the accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 15.09.2023 at about 04.20 p.m., she was proceeding on Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-06-EW- 7398, as a pillion rider along with her father and mother, and when they reached opposite Varin School Road, Tumkur-Kunigal SH-33,
Guluru-Village, Tumkur Taluk & District, a Skoda Car bearing Regn.No.KL-22- F-3285, driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the vehicle in which she was travelling.

Due to the accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and thereafter, she was shifted to Unnathi Multispeciality Hospital, Tumkur, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient and spent a sum of .1,00,000/- towards medicines, attendant, conveyance and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and was a student.
Due to the accidental injuries, petitioner has suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of car by its driver.
The respondents, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

3. In pursuance of notice, both the respondents appeared before the tribunal through their respective counsel and filed their separate written statement.
4.
In the Written Statement, the respondents have denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondents have also denied age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further respondents have also contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Further 1st respondent has contended that the Skoda car was insured with the 2nd respondent vide Policy No.76260131230100008624 valid from 27.08.2023 to 26.08.2024 and the policy was in force at the time of alleged accident.
Further the driver of vehicle was having valid driving license as on the date of accident.
The amount claimed by petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the petition.
5. Respondent No.2, in the written statement, has contended that the person who was driving the vehicle in question had no valid and effective driving license to drive Skoda car.
Further this Chandana .G vs Parfina Bapin .P
on 6 August, 2025

2 respondent has issued policy No.76260131230100008624 for the period from 27.08.2023 to 26.08.2024 in favour of first respondent and the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
The amount claimed by petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, this tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioner proves that, she sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 15.09.2023 at about 04.20 p.m., Opposite Varin School Road,
Tumakuru-Kunigal SH-33, Guluru Village, Tumakuru Taluk and District, while she was proceeding on a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-06-EW-7398 as a pillion rider,
due to the rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.KL-22-F-3285 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order or award?

7. In order to prove the contention of the petition, the Natural Guardian/mother of minor petitioner examined as PW.1, got examined Dr.Sreedhara.K.C., Consultant Neuro Physician &
Rehabilitation/Mental Health and MLC Consultant at Deepashri Hospital and Neuro Rehabilitation as PW.2 and MRO of Unnathi Multispeciality Hospital examined as PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to 19 and closed evidence of her side.
The respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary.

8. Heard the arguments of both side and perused the materials available on record.
9.

The petitioner has contended that on 15.09.2023 at about 04.20 p.m., accident occurred at opposite Varin School Road, Tumkur, Kunigal, SH-33, Guluru-Village, Tumkur Taluk and District, when she was proceeding on Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-06-EW-7398, as a Chandana .G vs Parfina Bapin .P

on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77775805/
3 pillion rider along with her father and mother, due to the rash and negligent driving of Skoda Car bearing Regn.No.KL-22-F-3285 by its driver in which she sustained grievous injuries.
11. In order to prove rash and negligent driving of Skoda Car bearing Regn.No.KL-22-F-3285 by its driver, the guardian of petitioner examined as PW.1.
In the chief examination, PW.1 has deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of car by its driver, the accident occurred.
On perusal of cross- examination of PW.1 nothing has been elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disprove the case of petitioner.
12. Further, in order to prove accident, the petitioner has produced first information statement which is marked as Ex.P.2.

On perusal of Ex.P.2, first information statement, the brother of petitioner by name Sri.Gangaraju S/o Guruvaiah has lodged a complaint with police on 16.09.2023 pertaining to the accident occurred on 15.09.2023.
The police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 337 of IPC.
In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle.
The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The petitioner also furnished spot Mahazar & sketch, which are marked as Ex.P.3 & 4.
The said documents disclose that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said document.
In the mahazar also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials to show that the actual facts at the place accident differ from facts as mentioned in sketch and mahazar.
Ex.P.5 is the IMV Report, wherein the damages caused to both the vehicles are mentioned.
The said document discloses the aspect of damages being caused to the offending car.
The driver or owner of offending car not explained the manner in which the vehicle got damaged.
The said document indicates the involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
Ex.P8 is the notice issued under Sec.133 of IMV Act and reply given to said notice is marked as Ex.P.9.
In the notice given by I.O, there is clear mention about involvement of offending vehicle and negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
Respondent No.1, owner of the car, has given reply to the notice as per Ex.P.9.
In the reply given by respondent No.1, there appears to be no denial about involvement of the vehicle in the accident and also negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The respondent No.1, being the owner of the car, is having opportunity to explain the manner of accident as well as damages caused to the vehicle vide reply notice.
But, respondent No.1 neither denied involvement of car in the accident nor denied negligence on the part of driver of the car in the cause of accident.
The said document also discloses the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
Ex.P.6 is the Wound certificate which discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner in the road traffic accident.
In the petition as well as evidence, petitioner stated about car colliding to the motorcycle from front side.
The materials on record disclose the aspect of collision between the vehicles from behind.
In the first information statement, it is stated that the driver of offending vehicle negligently stopped the vehicle due to which the accident is stated to have occurred.
The respondent No.1 not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or disprove the said contention.
Though the manner of accident is mentioned wrongly in the petition, same cannot be considered sufficient to doubt or dispute the cause of accident.
The wrong mentioning of manner of accident in the petition will not appear sufficient to consider that the accident has not taken place.

Chandana .G vs Parfina Bapin .P on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77775805/
4
The police records furnished by petitioner clearly indicate the aspect of occurring of accident and involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
The respondents not placed satisfactory materials to disprove or rebut the documents furnished by petitioner related to cause of accident.
The manner of accident is stated in the documents furnished by petitioner which has not been rebutted with cogent and substantive materials.

In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to doubt the occurrence of accident, the wrong mentioning of manner of accident cannot be considered sufficient to doubt or dispute the occurrence of accident.
The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 & 338 of IPC, which is marked at Ex.P.10.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.

In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondents and in the cross examination also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioners could be elicited.

No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioners pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
13. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
On perusal of records, it can be duly construed that negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle is the cause for the accident.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.10, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Skoda Car bearing Regn.No.KL-22-F-3285 by its driver and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:
In view of held issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.
15.
The petitioner contended that due to accident she sustained injuries and said injuries are grievous in nature.
In order to prove the injuries sustained by her, the guardian of petitioner produced wound certificate and discharge summary, which are marked at Ex.P.6 and 7.
On perusal of Ex.P.6 & 7 it reveals that, the petitioner sustained crush injury of lacerated wound on the right Chandana .G vs Parfina Bapin .P

on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77775805/
5 parietal region around 7cm and as per discharge summary, she sustained lacerated scalp wound with periorbital oedema and traumatic brain injury (TBI).

Further on examination, she found left periorbital oedema, abrasion over left supraorbital region, abrasion over left shoulder and lacerated scalp wound on left side and later discharged and she took treatment as an inpatient from 15.09.2023 to 19.09.2023 i.e., for a period of 05 days.
The respondent does not appear to have disputed the nature of injuries caused to the petitioner.
The respondent not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to disprove or disbelieve the documents furnished by the petitioner related to the injuries sustained by her.

16. PW.2/Doctor deposed in his evidence that, petitioner has sustained injury to head, periorbital oedema, abrasion over left supra orbital region, left shoulder, lacerated scalp wound over left side and she was treated conservatively and later discharged.
Further PW.2 deposed that petitioner come up with complaint of decreased activity, poor performance in studies, lack of concentration, poor interaction with other kids.

17. Further as per Neuro Psychological assessment report given by Mrs Sowmya reveals severe impairment of motor speed, focused attention, category of fluency, work memory, response inhibition, learning verbal memory, verbal comprehension visuospace construction, suggestive of pre frontal cortex, bilateral dorsolateral, temporal lobe, from lobe involvement advised cognitive retaining, neuro psychological profile suggestive Cognitive disability.
PW.2 examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
Further, the doctor also produced examination report, neuro psychological report, CT Scan report and X-ray, which are marked at Ex.P.14 to 17.
The doctor has assessed the disability to the whole body at 13.3%.
18. In the petition the age of the petitioner by name Baby Chandana.G is shown as 06 years.
In order to prove the age of the petitioner, notarized copy of Aadhaar Card is furnished which is marked as Ex.P.13, wherein date of birth of petitioner is mentioned as 26.09.2018.
As per the materials on record, the accident occurred on 15.09.2023.
The age of petitioner is 05 years as on the date of accident.
No contrary materials are being placed before the court in order to doubt or dispute the age of petitioner.
In the absence of materials to the contrary, the document furnished by the petitioner is to be considered for ascertaining the age.
On consideration of materials placed before the court, the age of the petitioner is considered to be 05 years as on the date of accident.
19. In Master Mallikarjun V/s Divisional Manager, The National Insurance Company Ltd and another, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follows:

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the disability is upto 10% to the whole body .1 lakh, above 10% and upto 30% to the whole body, .3 lakhs: upto 60%, .4 lakhs, Upto 90% .5 lakhs and above 90% it should be .6 lakhs.
For all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant etc.
20. Case on hand the doctor has given disability of 13.3% to the whole body.
As per Master Mallikarjun case from 10 to 30% - .3 lakhs.

Accordingly the petitioner is entitled for .3,00,000/-
under the head pain and suffering already undergone and to be suffered in future, mental and Chandana .G vs Parfina Bapin

6
physical shock, hardship, inconvenience, and discomforts etc and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability.

21. Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that she has spent more than .1,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance and transportation charges.
The petitioner has produced Inpatient bill at Ex.P.11 for .55,800/- and also produced advance receipts marked at Ex.P.12.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials to rebut or disprove the medical bills furnished by the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for .55,800/- under the head medical and incidental expenses during the period of hospitalization.

22. Towards loss of income during treatment:
The petitioner has contended that she was student and she has been hospitalized due to the injuries sustained by her in the Road Traffic Accident.
So, when the father/mother of the petitioner was in the hospital along with petitioner, she has no income for her livelihood during that period.

As such the petitioner is entitled for lump sum of .50,000/-
under the head Discomfort, inconvenience and loss of earnings to the parents during the period of hospitalization.

23. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:

24.

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs.
Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the petitioner is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

sentences.text: 25. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondents No.1 and 2.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Skoda Car bearing Regn.No.KL-22-F-3285 by its driver.
There appears to be no dispute pertaining to the ownership of respondent No.1 over the vehicle and about issue of policy pertaining to the vehicle by respondent No.2.
The materials on record disclose that the policy of insurance was valid and effective and the driver of offending vehicle was having valid and effective licence at the time of accident.

So, the respondent No.1 & 2,
being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
26. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of MV Act is allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of .4,05,800/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Five Thousand Eight Hundred only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

Entire compensation amount shall be kept in FD in the name of minor petitioner in any of the Nationalized Bank or Scheduled Bank of the choice of minor guardian for a period of 3 years or till she attain the age of majority whichever is later.
The guardian of petitioner is entitled to receive interest that accrues on FD periodically.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal.

Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to his account after expiry of three years period of deposit, without waiting for further order of court.
Advocates' fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Entire compensation amount shall be kept in FD in the name of minor petitioner in any of the Nationalized Bank or Scheduled Bank of the choice of minor guardian for a period of 3 years or till she attain the age of majority whichever is later.
The guardian of petitioner is entitled to receive interest that accrues on FD periodically.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal.
Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to his account after expiry of three years period of deposit, without waiting for further order of court.
Advocates' fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
